78:1: Interpretation of Surat An-Naba In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty says, denouncing the polytheists’ questioning of the Day of Resurrection, denying that it will happen: About what are they asking one another? * About the Great report. That is, what are they asking about regarding the matter of Resurrection, which is the Great report, meaning the tremendous, terrifying, dazzling report. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: The Great report is the resurrection after death. Mujahid said: It is the Qur’an. The first is more evident because He says: about which they differ. That is, people have two opinions about it: a believer in it and a disbeliever. Then God the Almighty says, threatening those who deny the al-Qiyamah 75:“By no means, they will know. Then by no means, they will know.” This is a severe threat and a definite warning. Then God the Almighty proceeded to explain His great power to create strange things and wondrous matters, which indicate His power over whatever He wills regarding the matter of the Resurrection and other matters. He says: Have We not made the earth a bed? That is, smoothed out for the creatures, subservient to them, stable, still, and the mountains pegs? That is, He made them pegs for it, anchoring them with them, making them firm and steady until they became still and did not shake with those on them. Then the Almighty said: And We created you in pairs, meaning male and female, each of whom enjoys the other and procreation occurs through that, as He said: And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them, and He has put between you affection and mercy. And the Almighty said: And We have made your sleep a rest, meaning a cessation of movement so that you may rest from the frequent going back and forth and striving to make a living during the day. A similar verse was presented in Surat Al-Furqan. And We have made the night a covering, meaning that it covers people with its darkness and blackness, as He said: And the night when it covers it. And the poet said: When they were dressed for the night, she set up for him from her ears, while he was leaning forward. Qatada said about the verse of God the Almighty: {And We have made the night as a covering} meaning a resting place. And His verse: {And We have made the day for livelihood} meaning We made it bright, luminous and shining so that people can move about in it and go and come for livelihood, earning a living, trading and other things. And His verse: {And We constructed above you seven strong heavens} meaning the seven heavens in their vastness, height, perfection, mastery and adornment with fixed and moving planets. For this reason God the Almighty said: {And We made a blazing lamp} meaning the sun that illuminates the entire world and whose light glows for all the people of the earth. And the Almighty said: And We sent down from the pressed clouds abundant water. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The pressed clouds are the winds. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed told us, Abu Dawud al-Hafri told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Minhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We sent down from the pressed clouds, he said: The winds. And this is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Kalbi, Zaid bin Aslam and his son Abd al-Rahman said, They are the winds. The meaning of this statement is that they bring rain from the clouds. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, From the pressed clouds, meaning from the clouds. This is what Ikrimah also said, as did Abu al-Aaliyah, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and al-Thawri, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Al-Farra’ said: They are the clouds that are milked with rain but have not yet rained, just as a woman is said to be Mu’sar when her period is approaching but she has not yet menstruated. On the authority of Al-Hasan and Qatadah: From the pressed clouds meaning the heavens. This is a strange statement. What is more apparent is that what is meant by the pressed clouds are the clouds, as God Almighty said: God is He who sends the winds, and they stir up the clouds and spreads them in the sky however He wills and makes them into fragments, and you see the rain emerge from within them. That is, from between them. And the saying of the Most High: Pour-down water. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Pour-down water. Ath-Thawri said: Consecutive. Ibn Zayd said: A lot. Ibn Jarir said: “Thaj is not known in the speech of the Arabs as a description of abundance. Rather, thaj is the continuous pouring. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The best of Hajj is the pouring of blood.” He meant pouring the blood of the body. This is what he said. I said: And in the hadith of the woman with istihadah when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Should I describe to you the karsaf? He meant that she should stuff herself with cotton. She said: “O Messenger of God, it is more than that. Rather, it pours abundantly.” This indicates the use of thaj to mean continuous, abundant pouring. And God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: That We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens of thriving. That is, We may bring forth with this abundant, good, beneficial, blessed water grain that is stored up for people and livestock, and vegetation, that is, greenery that is eaten fresh, and gardens, that is, orchards and gardens of various fruits of different colors, tastes, and smells, even if they are gathered in one spot on the earth. That is why He said gardens of thriving. Ibn Abbas and others said: Gardens of thriving. This is like the Almighty’s saying: “And on the earth are neighboring tracts and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, some of them twined and some untied, watered by a single water. And We make some of them excel others in food. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.”

78:17: God Almighty says, informing us about the Day of Judgment, that it is timed to a specified term that cannot be increased or decreased, and no one knows its exact time except God Almighty, as He Almighty says: And We do not delay it except for a specified term. “The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come in groups.” Mujahid said: In groups. Al-Bukhari said: The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come in groups. Muhammad told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Between the two Trumpets will be forty.’ They said: ‘Forty days?’ He said: ‘No.’ They said: ‘Forty months?’ He said: ‘No.’ They said: ‘Forty years?’ He said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘Then God will send down water from the sky, and they will grow as plants grow. There will be nothing of the human being that will not decay except one bone, which is the coccyx.’” The creation will ride on the Day of Resurrection. And the heaven was opened and became doors meaning paths and routes for the angels to descend. And the mountains were set in motion and became a mirage as in the Almighty’s saying: And you will see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the clouds pass and as in His saying: And the mountains will be like carded wool and He said here: and became a mirage meaning it will appear to the observer that they are a thing when they are not. After this, they will disappear completely, leaving no trace or trace, as in the Almighty’s saying: “And they ask you about the mountains. Say, ‘My Lord will blow them away with a blast.’ He will leave them as a level plain. You will not see therein any crookedness or unevenness.” And the Almighty said: And the Day We set the mountains in motion and you will see the earth appearing as a place of rest. And the Almighty said: Indeed, Hell will be an ambush meaning an ambush prepared for the transgressors meaning the rebellious, disobedient ones who oppose the messengers as a place of return meaning a place of return, turning back, destination, and lodging. Al-Hasan and Qatada said regarding the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, Hell is ever lying in wait, meaning that no one will enter Paradise until he passes through the Fire. If he has a pass, he will be saved, otherwise he will be detained. Sufyan al-Thawri said: There are three bridges over it. Both of them were narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Suddi said: Remaining therein for ages means seven hundred ages, each age seventy years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day like a thousand years of what you count. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was abrogated by the words of God Almighty: So taste [the punishment], for We will not increase you except in torment. Khalid bin Ma'dan said: This verse and the saying of God the Almighty: Except what your Lord wills about the people of monotheism were both narrated by Ibn Jarir. He told us that the period is eighty years, and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said, They will remain there for ages. Only God Almighty knows the number of these periods. He told us that one period is eighty years, and a year is three hundred and sixty days, and every day is like a thousand years of what you count. Ibn Jarir also narrated both of them. As for scalding water, it is the hot water whose heat and scorching heat have reached the end, and purulent water is what has accumulated from the pus, sweat, tears, and wounds of the people of Hell. It is cold and its coldness cannot be tolerated and its stench cannot be confronted. We have already discussed purulent water in Surat Sad in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. May God protect us from that by His grace and generosity. Ibn Jarir said: It was said that what is meant by His saying: They will not taste therein any coolness means sleep, as Al-Kindi said: Her sheets cooled on me, so the cold pushed me away from her and her kisses. God the Almighty said: A just recompense meaning this punishment that they have reached is according to their corrupt deeds that they used to do in this world. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah and others. His saying completely means completely denial, and it is a verbal noun derived from a non-verb. They said: A Bedouin was heard asking al-Farra’ on al-Marwah: Is shaving or cutting short hair more preferable to you? Some of them recited: You have long discouraged me from my companions and from the shortest of their needs for healing. And the Almighty said: And everything We have recorded in a book meaning, We have known the deeds of all the servants and have written them down for them, and We will reward them for that, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. And the Almighty said: Then taste, for We will not increase you except in punishment meaning, it will be said to the people of Hell: Taste what you are in, for We will not increase you except in punishment of the same kind, and another of its kind in pairs. He said: They will be in more punishment forever. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mus`ab al-Suri told us, Khalid ibn `Abd al-Rahman told us, Jasr ibn Farqad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: I asked Abu Barzah al-Aslami about the most severe verse in the Book of God for the people of Hell. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite: Then taste, for We will not increase you except in punishment. He said: The people were destroyed by their disobedience to God, the Almighty. Jasr ibn Farqad is completely weak in hadith.

Its ancient and modern forms, such as the Almighty’s saying: And they will find what they did present, and His saying: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and left behind, and And the disbeliever will say, ‘Oh, I wish I were dust,’ meaning, the disbeliever will wish on that day that he had been dust in this world and had never been created or come into existence.
